factual_methodology.summary: Historical contracts, Rothschild Archive, Brazilian issues, institutional records and specialist histories used with qualified conclusions; unsupported conspiracy claims rejected.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Multiple generations, sovereign credit, historical political conditions, actual contractual authority and distributional effects developed as continuous research prose.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Two bilingual-parallel analytical quantitative charts with distinct measurement caveats, historical chronology, causal flow and geographic evidence map.

evidence_traceability.summary: Documentary Rothschild Archive and state sources with aligned bilingual citation URLs and numeric charts.

counterfactual_review.summary: Rejects unverified dynastic continuous corporate control and tests banking risk, repayment and institutional authority alternatives.

limitations: Surviving accounting ledgers do not establish a modern consolidated net worth
Contractual access does not prove unlimited political control
notes: Substantive historical rewrite, including Frankfurt, family partnerships, Napoleon-era bullion transfers, Brazilian sovereign bonds of 1824-29 and infrastructure financing, 1875 Suez and differences between economic influence and public power. Removed editorial afterword.
